text.p: Financial publishing house Euromoney Publications Plc widened its horizons on Wednesday by buying its rival Institutional Investor Inc for 84 million pounds ($140.8 million).
"We think it will be a very good fit," Padriac Fallon, Euromoney's chairman, told Reuters, adding Institutional Investor had "a wonderful brand name".

Institutional Investor (II), which publishes two editions of the magazine of the same name and has 23 newsletters and a conference division, had been on the market for some time. It is being bought from ABC Inc, a subsidiary of the Walt Disney Co, for cash.

"II has got a jewel of a newsletter business," Fallon said, adding it made up a significant part of total business at the group. "We prize that. It is a base to create an international business from," he added.

Pearson Plc, which owns the Financial Times newspaper and the Thompson Financial Publishing Group, with its own financial magazines, newsletters and screen-based services, had been seen as other potential suitors.
Euromoney had not made any definite plans for any of the Institutional Investor products, but there was limited overlap, Fallon said.
Only Institutional Investor's international edition overlapped with Euromoney in terms of advertising.

"The only area of overlap and direct competition is between Euromoney and the international edition of II," Fallon said, adding both were profitable. II's international edition has a controlled circulation of 45,000 compared with its domestic run of 100,000.

Staff at the U.S. firm will have to wait to hear about management changes as Euromoney, while maintaining an open mind on those currently in charge, is not likely to decide on their roles for a few months, Fallon said.

There have been questions over whether Euromoney would keep II's international edition if it bought the company and how it would alter the newsletter division. But Fallon insisted decision-making would be kept in New York, saying he wanted to ensure "good stable U.S. management" for the group's expanded U.S. operation rather than British managers parachuting in.
He also ruled out merging or closing down the international edition of Institutional Investor. "The least likely outcome would be to shut it down".
Euromoney's confidence in the potential for the combination is underlined by the fact it is taking on $150 million in debt, the first time it has done so, to pay for Institutional Investor.

The acquisition requires shareholder approval but Euromoney's largest holder Associated Newspapers -- which has 72.5 percent of its equity -- said it supports the move, which will be approved at an EGM.
Fallon said most of Institutional Investor's business and revenues arose in the U.S. while Euromoney's were internationally generated.
Euromoney made record pre-tax profits of 12 million pounds for the half year to the end of March. It said Institutional Investor's revenues had grown and profitability had improved during 1997.

In 1995 Institutional Investor reported operating profits of 40.1 million pounds and in 1996 this rose to 44.0 million pounds. Its un-audited net liabilities, excluding net liabilities to be retained by ABC, were 8.6 million pounds, Euromoney said.
